newsitem.title: GERMANY: Forwarders more flexible than integrators -Airbus.
newsitem.headline: Forwarders more flexible than integrators -Airbus.

text.p: Freight forwarders can often provide better solutions than integrators for small goods, a leading European shipper said.
Arnaud Martin, Airbus Industrie's transport director, said integrators offered the best networks for very small parcels under 5kg but tended to be inflexible in their services.

Integrators are companies such as Federal Express and DHL, which attempt to control all aspects of the freight delivery process using their own staff, aircraft, vehicles and reservations systems, and track and trace delivery progress.

Martin's company now worked mostly with a handful of chosen forwarder partners in its restructured global small parcels distribution system for aircraft spare parts, he told the eighth World Express & Mail conference in Frankfurt.
"Standard freight forwarders have now largely improved their performance in the small parcels segment and are able to give the same quality as integrators," he said.

Martin added: "We have reduced from 13 suppliers (of freight services) down to four or five. But I do not see the opportunity to reduce to one because I do not see one company which can do everything."
Airbus now worked closely with forwarders such as Danzas and Emery as well as with DHL, he told Reuters later.
The four worldwide Airbus spare parts centres were responsible for organising their own freight movements according to their local needs, Martin said.
Large aircraft pieces were transported directly between European production sites in the company's A300-600ST (Super Transport) aircraft, known as "Beluga", he added.

Tha Airbus aircraft manufacturing consortium comprises Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale of France, British Aerospace Plc BA.L, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
